Privacy Policy

Effective: October 1, 2026

This Privacy Policy explains how Samir Kumar Shah, publishing Unsend under the Typhoon Labs name (“we,” “us,” or “our”) collects, uses, discloses, and protects information when you use the Unsend mobile application and related support pages (together, the “Service”).

1. Information we process

Private drafts and release effects

Text that you write and release using the private shred, burn, or dissolve options is processed on your device for the release effect and is not uploaded to our community database. We do not intentionally collect that text.

Anonymous account and public community content

After you choose Continue on the first-use Explore screen, Supabase creates a persistent anonymous account identifier and stores its session on your device. No public name is displayed. The internal pseudonymous author identifier is included in the data returned for approved posts and replies and may link a person's contributions. We use it for blocking, deletion, moderation, and abuse prevention. If you submit a post, we collect its text, selected category, author identifier, content identifier, submission time, and review status. Replies also include their text, author identifier, related post identifier, time, and status. Submissions become public only after review and approval.

Reports, blocks, and moderation information

If you report a post or reply, we collect the selected reason, reported content identifier, reporter identifier, report status, and time. We store which anonymous contributor identifiers you block so their content can be hidden for you. We may create internal moderation notes about actions taken.

Usage counters and reactions

We record up to one post opening and one “I hear you” reaction per anonymous account per post, and maintain public totals and visible reply counts. These totals do not represent named people. We also keep limited submission events to enforce daily posting and reporting limits.

Technical information

Our hosting and database provider may automatically process technical data needed to deliver and protect the Service, such as IP address, request time, device or browser information, and security logs. We do not use this data for advertising or cross-app tracking.

Support communications

If you contact us, we receive the information you provide, such as your email address, message, and attachments.

2. How we use information

  • Provide public posts, replies, sorting, categories, and usage counts.
  • Operate, maintain, secure, and troubleshoot the Service.
  • Review reports and enforce our Terms and Community Guidelines.
  • Respond to support, privacy, and content-removal requests.
  • Comply with legal obligations and protect people, rights, and the Service.

3. Public information

Posts and replies submitted to Explore are public. Although Unsend does not display a name or account, the content itself may identify you or another person. Do not submit personal information. We cannot control how other people copy, save, quote, or share public content.

4. Service providers and disclosures

We use Supabase to host the community database and process public posts, replies, reports, counters, and related technical data. When enabled, Cloudflare Turnstile processes browser and device signals during anonymous signup to help prevent automated abuse. We use Expo and its EAS services to build and distribute the app. Apple may process information when you obtain or use the app through its services. These providers process information under their own terms and privacy notices.

We may disclose information when reasonably necessary to comply with law, respond to valid legal process, investigate fraud or security issues, enforce our agreements, protect safety or rights, or complete a business transfer such as a merger or acquisition.

We do not sell personal information. We do not use community content for targeted advertising or cross-app tracking.

5. Legal bases

Where applicable law requires a legal basis, we process information to perform our agreement with you, pursue legitimate interests such as operating and securing the Service, comply with law, and, where required, with your consent.

6. Retention

Public posts and replies remain available until deleted by you or us. Pending content remains until reviewed or removed. Reports and moderation records are retained as reasonably needed to handle abuse, document enforcement, and protect the Service. Anonymous accounts older than 90 days may be removed automatically only if their last sign-in was over 90 days ago and they have no authored posts, replies, reports, saved blocks, reactions, or views in the last 90 days. Support communications are retained as reasonably needed to resolve requests and meet legal obligations. Technical logs are retained according to our providers' settings and legitimate security needs.

7. Your choices and rights

You can avoid collection of community content by using only the private release options. In the app, My submissions lets you delete pending or approved posts and replies; About also lets you unblock contributors and delete your anonymous account and authored content. Deleting the app does not automatically delete public content. Delete your account first or contact support. You may also request removal or exercise applicable privacy rights by emailing typhoon.lab.app@gmail.com. Include enough information to locate older content, but do not send identity documents unless requested.

Depending on where you live, you may have rights to access, correct, delete, restrict, object to, or obtain a copy of personal information, and to appeal a denied request. You may also complain to your local data-protection authority. We aim to respond within 30 days, or within the period required by applicable law.

8. Children

The Service is not directed to children under 13, or a higher minimum age where local law requires it. We do not knowingly collect personal information from a child below the applicable minimum age. Contact us if you believe a child has provided personal information so we can review and remove it.

9. International processing

We and our providers may process information in the United States and other countries. Where required, appropriate safeguards are used for international transfers.

10. Security

We use reasonable administrative and technical measures intended to protect information. No storage or transmission system is completely secure, and we cannot guarantee absolute security.

11. Changes

We may update this policy. We will change the effective date and provide additional notice in the app or on this page when required.
